compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`outbound_field_diff.py` wires the live account-search resolver into the outbound mapper by **setting
an attribute on it**:

    outbound_mapper._assignee_resolver = lambda lv: assignee_resolver(lv, jira_key)

wrapped in a `try/except (AttributeError, TypeError): pass`. Consumers then **discover** it with
`getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` and silently fall back to a non-authoritative result when
it is absent.

This is a collaborator passed by side-channel rather than by contract, and it has three concrete costs:

1. **It fails silently.** If the injection ever stops happening — a mapper that forbids attribute assignment
   hits the bare `except ...: pass` — every assignee resolution degrades to `authoritative=False`. That is not
   cosmetic: a permanently non-authoritative assignee makes the outbound diff re-emit an assignee change it can
   never converge, the churn class epic `ace2` exists to fix.
2. **It hid a real bug in review.** GitHub PR #120's proposed Data Center adapter copied the `getattr` line
   into a class where nothing ever set the attribute, so its ENTIRE authoritative branch was dead code and DC
   would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. A typed constructor parameter makes that
   failure impossible to write.
3. **It is invisible to the type checker.** Each assignment needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` because the
   attribute is on no Protocol, so mypy cannot see the dependency at all.

## The FULL live site list (re-enumerated against this tree)

The Data Center adapter has since MERGED, so the blast radius is wider than "one injection + one getattr".
`grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` currently matches, in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

| # | site | role |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `outbound_field_diff.py:270` | core injection (`try/except`, per-`jira_key` closure) |
| 2 | `adapters/jira/backend.py:111` | Cloud `_JiraOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 3 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:118` | **DC** `_DCOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 4 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:331` | **DC** `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` injection onto `self.outbound`, `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` |
| — | `adapters/jira/backend.py:105,115`, `jira_datacenter/backend.py:115,324`, `jira_datacenter/_people.py:50` | docstrings that describe the attribute |
| — | `outbound_differ.py:384` | an UNRELATED local function that happens to share the name; leave it (renaming it is churn, and it is a nested `def`, not an attribute) |

Two implementers of the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` therefore have to change, not one:
`adapters/jira/backend.py:92` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:109` (DC).

The two injections have DIFFERENT lifecycles, which is the one thing that needs a decision rather than a
transcription:

- the core injection (#1) is built per remote key inside `compute_update_fields` and is the resolver the
  differ means to use;
- DC's (#4) is bound once in the backend constructor to the `jira.JIRA` client
  (`lambda name: _search_users_by_username(client, name)`), with no `jira_key`.

Today the core injection **overwrites** DC's constructor one whenever the differ runs, so "core wins,
constructor is the fallback" is not a new policy — it is exactly the current behaviour, and the explicit
form must preserve it.

Also note the call site is NOT where the injection is: `resolve_assignee` is invoked at
`outbound_field_diff.py:398` inside `diff_canonical_fields`, a function that today receives no resolver.
`compute_update_fields` (the injection point) calls it at line ~271, so the resolver has to be threaded
through that hop as well.

## Approach

Thread the resolver **explicitly** instead of by attribute:

1. Widen the neutral port `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` in `_backend.py` with a keyword-only,
   defaulted `assignee_resolver` parameter, so the dependency appears in the contract and is typechecked.
2. Widen BOTH implementers to accept and forward it:
   - Cloud `adapters/jira/backend.py` → `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=assignee_resolver)`, deleting the getattr;
   - DC `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` → `NameIdentity(resolver=...)`, deleting the getattr.
3. Give DC's `_DCOutbound` a declared, typed constructor parameter for its client-bound resolver, and have
   `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` pass it there — deleting the `self.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`
   assignment and its `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`. `resolve_assignee` prefers the explicit parameter and
   falls back to the constructor-supplied one, which reproduces today's overwrite semantics exactly.
4. Thread the resolver from `compute_update_fields` through `diff_canonical_fields` to the
   `resolve_assignee` call, and delete the attribute-injection block (and its `try/except ... : pass`).
5. Update the four/five docstrings that describe the attribute, and the test doubles that implement
   `resolve_assignee` so they accept the new keyword.
6. Keep every observable resolution outcome identical — this is plumbing.

### What "resolver absent" means, explicitly

The new parameter's default is `assignee_resolver=None`, and `None` keeps its CURRENT documented meaning:
"no live account search is available on this path", which the identity models already define as the
permissive, non-authoritative string match — `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=None).resolve("a@x.com",
{"account_id": "acct-9"}) == ("a@x.com", False, False)`, pinned today by
`test_user_identity_heldout.test_cloud_with_no_resolver_keeps_the_permissive_fallback`. The change is
not the VALUE but its provenance: absence becomes a **declared default on the contract** that a caller
chooses, instead of the invisible outcome of an injection that silently did not happen. Nothing raises,
and no outcome moves.

## Why this is a separate ticket

Discovered while implementing story J4 [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], whose plan asserted the attribute was never
set (true of PR #120, not of this tree) and whose AC4 asked for `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` to return
nothing. Satisfying that literally means changing the **backend-neutral port signature**, which affects every
backend — a materially wider blast radius than J4's three-file scope, and precisely the kind of core-risking
change epic e369 deliberately sequenced away from the Data Center delivery path. J4 instead guarantees the
property where it matters (the new identity models take the resolver as an explicit parameter and contain no
`getattr` discovery at all) and defers this core cleanup here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` matches nothing except the unrelated local function in
      `outbound_differ.py`, and no `getattr(..., "_assignee_resolver", ...)` remains anywhere — in
      particular all four sites above are gone
- [ ] the resolver is a declared parameter on the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` contract in
      `_backend.py`, and on BOTH implementers (Cloud and DC)
- [ ] no `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` remains at either wiring site, and `make typecheck` passes
- [ ] the six-state parity oracle in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_heldout.py`
      (`_CLOUD_STATES` × `test_account_id_identity_matches_the_live_cloud_backend_state_for_state`)
      still passes and still compares the live backend against the live identity model. Its ONE line
      that builds `expected` by attribute-injection (`backend.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`,
      line ~148) necessarily becomes the explicit parameter pass — that seam is what this ticket
      deletes, so the oracle cannot be literally byte-unmodified. Its six states, its expectations,
      and its live-vs-live construction stay exactly as they are; only the injection line changes
      form. Every OTHER assertion about `resolve_assignee`
      (`state/test_canonical_mapper_surface.py`, `test_backend_characterization.py`,
      `test_dc_backend_characterization.py`) passes UNMODIFIED
- [ ] a test proves the degradation path is gone: with the resolver absent, the behavior is the documented
      explicit default rather than a silent non-authoritative fallback
- [ ] a test proves DC still resolves authoritatively through its constructor-supplied resolver, and that a
      core-supplied resolver takes precedence over it (today's overwrite semantics, preserved)

file_impact.reason: widen the neutral OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee contract to declare the resolver parameter
delete the attribute-injection block and pass the resolver explicitly at the call site
drop the getattr discovery in favour of the declared parameter
J1 pins all six resolve_assignee states and must pass unmodified
